question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Child’s play
solution:
The correct answer is '**An easy task**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** meaning for the given idiom '**Child's play**' is '**An easy task**'.
 
• **Child's play**: to be very easy
 
 
• ***E.g. **Using computers nowadays is child's play.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at some similar idioms.
 
 
• **It's a piece of cake**: something easily done

 
 
• *For him, taking tests is a piece of cake.*
 
 
 
• **A walk in the park**: something that is very easy to accomplish
 
 
• *As any director will tell you, doing Shakespeare isn't a walk in the park.*
 
 
 
• **It's a cinch**: an easy thing to do
 
 
• *It sounds difficult, but compared to full-time work it was a cinch.*
